meta.source_document: City of Phoenix 2026 Heat Response Plan DRAFT (2.13.2026)
meta.quote_verification: every source_text verified verbatim against its stated page

claims.source_text: Historical development patterns and varying topography across Phoenix lead to neighborhood-to-neighborhood air temperature differences of 10°F or more on summer days.
claims.test: Measure the spread of daily mean 2 m temperature across the 15 urban villages on each day of the study window and compare with 10 degF.

claims.source_text: In 2025, 37% of heat-related deaths in Maricopa County occurred on days with the HeatRisk was designated by the National Weather Service as Major or Extreme, and 63% of deaths occurred on days when the HeatRisk was designated as Moderate, Minor, or None.
claims.test: Not testable with temperature data alone. Recorded because it is the plan's own statement that most heat deaths fall outside warning conditions.

clauses.source_text: Protective directives are implemented when temperatures exceed 105°F, deploying additional resources and implementing enhanced rehabilitation measures.
clauses.action: Activate summer heat protocols including cold immersion techniques
clauses.extraction_note: Explicit numeric trigger. Scope recorded as citywide: the plan attaches no geography to the condition.
clauses.strategy: Equip first responders for effective heat response

clauses.source_text: During the heat season, outreach teams are equipped with heat relief kits to distribute to community members in need, including water, hats, cooling towels, and other essential supplies.
clauses.action: Equip Homeless Outreach Teams with Cooling Resources
clauses.not_evaluable_reason: Activated for the heat season; no thermal condition stated.
actor_full: Office of Heat Response and Mitigation
clauses.strategy: Equip first responders for effective heat response

clauses.source_text: 17 City of Phoenix Library locations served as Cooling Centers throughout the 2025 Heat Season and the City will continue this commitment in 2025.

actor_full: Office of Heat Response and Mitigation

clauses.source_text: Each unit must be able to safely cool all livable rooms to 86°F when using evaporative cooling and 82°F when using air conditioning.
clauses.action: Promote and Enforce Cooling Ordinance for Rental Housing Units (evaporative cooling standard)
clauses.extraction_note: One sentence carries two thresholds; split into two clauses.
clauses.not_evaluable_reason: Indoor habitability standard. FortyGuard measures 2 m outdoor air, so this cannot be evaluated directly without an indoor model.
clauses.strategy: Support cool and safe home environments

clauses.source_text: Each unit must be able to safely cool all livable rooms to 86°F when using evaporative cooling and 82°F when using air conditioning.
clauses.action: Promote and Enforce Cooling Ordinance for Rental Housing Units (air conditioning standard)
clauses.extraction_note: Second threshold from the same sentence.
clauses.not_evaluable_reason: Indoor habitability standard; not an outdoor trigger.
clauses.strategy: Support cool and safe home environments

clauses.source_text: The City will partner with the Red Cross and the Arizona Mobile and Manufactured Homeowners Association to coordinate a volunteer-led outreach program for residents of mobile and manufactured homes as well as seniors.
clauses.action: Deploy Heat Outreach Teams to Mobile Home and Senior Communities
clauses.not_evaluable_reason: Outreach campaign. Targets a heat-vulnerable population but is not conditioned on temperature.
actor_full: Office of Heat Response and Mitigation
clauses.strategy: Support cool and safe home environments

clauses.source_text: Volunteers from the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) and Park Stewards are stationed every Saturday and Sunday from 7-10 a.m. at entrances to trails that have higher rates of heat-related illnesses and/or those where rescue operations are more technically complex, including trails at Camelback Mountain, Piestewa Peak, and South Mountain.
clauses.action: Deploy Outreach Teams to Select Trailheads
clauses.not_evaluable_reason: Fixed weekend schedule, 7-10 a.m., May through September. The deployment window is a clock, not a condition.
actor_full: Office of Heat Response and Mitigation
clauses.strategy: Support cool and safe mobility and recreation

clauses.source_text: The program restricts access to select trails when the National Weather Service issues an Extreme Heat Warning.
clauses.action: Close Select Trailheads on Extreme Heat Warning Days
clauses.extraction_note: The plan states no temperature for this trigger; the condition is defined by another agency and issued for a whole forecast zone. A 110 degF proxy is used, anchored to the plan's own pairing on page 6: 'hit at least 110°F on 37 days and there were 31 days with National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warnings in effect'. 37 vs 31 days means the mapping is close but not exact, hence reduced confidence. Treat results for this clause as indicative.
clauses.strategy: Support cool and safe mobility and recreation

clauses.strategy: Support cool and safe mobility and recreation

clauses.source_text: The Human Resources Safety & Worker's Compensation Division has developed written Heat Injury and Illness Prevention Plans with departments whose employees face heat safety dangers during their work duties.

clauses.source_text: The ordinance requires these businesses to have compliant heat safety plans that ensure appropriate measures to protect employees are in place.
clauses.action: Promote and Enforce Heat Safety Ordinance for City Contractors

actor_full: Office of Heat Response and Mitigation
clauses.strategy: Educate the community and engage with partners

clauses.source_text: Temperatures at Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport hit at least 110°F on 37 days and there were 31 days with National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warnings in effect.
clauses.action: Season-severity benchmark: daily high at or above 110 degF
clauses.extraction_note: The plan measures season severity from one station, named in the sentence. This is the citywide-sensing assumption, stated explicitly.
actor_full: Office of Heat Response and Mitigation

clauses.source_text: Nighttime temperatures failed to drop below 90°F at Sky Harbor on 23 days, including a seasonal high overnight low of 95°F on July 10.
clauses.action: Season-severity benchmark: overnight low at or above 90 degF
clauses.extraction_note: Overnight heat is where the urban heat island is strongest, so this benchmark is the most spatially variable one in the document.
actor_full: Office of Heat Response and Mitigation

clauses.source_text: The table below presents weekly averages, ranges, and probabilities of exceedance based on 2016-2025 observations from Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport.
clauses.action: Planning benchmark: daily high at or above 100 degF
clauses.extraction_note: Threshold read from the column header '100°F or above' of the page 7 planning table; the quoted sentence establishes the table's source and station. Confidence reduced because the number is tabular, not prose.
actor_full: Office of Heat Response and Mitigation
